title: A performance review turns into an ambush
lede: You expected a routine review. Instead there is a document with dated allegations you have never heard before, and a phrase like "this is informal at this stage." Someone from HR is taking notes.

blocks.text: You expected a routine review. Instead there is a document with dated allegations you have never heard before, and a phrase like "this is informal at this stage." Someone from HR is taking notes.

items: "Informal" almost never means informal. This is usually step one of a process that has already been drafted to its conclusion.
Undocumented complaints appearing all at once means someone has been collecting rather than managing. That is itself significant.
Everything you say in this room can be written down. Nothing you say will change today's outcome, which was decided before you walked in.
Your instinct to defend each point individually is a trap. It makes you look like someone with many problems rather than someone being managed out.

items.move: Ask what the meeting formally is
items.detail: Informal chat, formal capability, disciplinary, or investigation. The answer determines your rights, including representation.

items.move: Do not respond to the substance today
items.detail: Say you want to answer properly and in writing. Nobody sensible objects to that, and refusal is itself informative.

items.move: Ask for the document and the notes
items.detail: Request a copy of the allegations, the notes of the meeting, and the chance to correct them.

items.move: Write your own note within the hour
items.detail: Who was there, what was alleged, what was said, exact phrases. Memory degrades fastest in the first day.
Emails showing approvals, changed priorities, missing resources, praise received. Forward nothing to a personal address without checking policy.

items.move: Get advice before the next meeting
items.detail: Union rep, employment adviser, or a lawyer. One consultation now is worth more than ten after the outcome.

items.say: "Before we go further — is this a formal process? If so, I would like to know which one and whether I can be accompanied."
"I want to give you a serious answer rather than a defensive one. Can you send me this in writing and I will respond by Friday?"
"I hear that you want a reaction now. I would rather be accurate. I am not going to comment on specifics today."
"For the notes: I am hearing several of these for the first time in this meeting."

items: Arguing every bullet point in the room. It concedes the frame and produces quotable material.
Crying "unfair" without specifics. Say instead: not raised at the time, not documented, not within my control.
Signing anything, including a note that says you have "read and understood."
Resigning in the meeting. It converts a possible settlement into nothing at all.
Emailing colleagues about it. Company systems are readable and it will be characterised as creating unrest.
Respond in writing, calmly, point by point, with dates and evidence. This document is your real defence.
Ask for a written improvement plan with measurable criteria. Vague plans exist to be failed.
Update your CV and speak to two contacts this week regardless of outcome. Optionality reduces panic more than reassurance does.
Watch for retaliation markers: work removed, meetings cancelled, exclusion from threads. Log them.

limit: If this followed a complaint you raised, a protected disclosure, a pregnancy, a disability disclosure, or a discrimination report, stop improvising. That pattern has specific legal weight in most jurisdictions and needs professional advice immediately.
